title: DumpDetective Observation
description: The fusion wire format: DumpDetective.Sdk.Observations.Observation as it actually serializes today via System.Text.Json with { PropertyNamingPolicy = CamelCase, Converters = { JsonStringEnumConverter } } — the exact options TraceReportWriter uses to write report.json (src/DumpDetective.Cli/Output/TraceReportWriter.cs). Verified empirically against a live build of DumpDetective.Sdk, not hand-derived from the C# source alone — see the 'Wire-format notes' below for the non-obvious results of that check. This is the real, shipped shape of trace-session report.json's `observations` array today; it is not a forward-looking design document. 2.0.0 (2026-09-10) is a breaking change from 1.0.0: ArtifactId/Capability/ObservationId now serialize as bare JSON strings instead of one-key wrapper objects (see the review that found this, docs/refactor/modularity/phase-1-sdk-review-findings.md item 8) — no real consumer existed for either shape yet, so this was the correct time to fix it, not a migration anyone needs to plan around.
notes: NOTE 1 — mixed casing: PropertyNamingPolicy.CamelCase only renames property *names* (id, observationType, ...). Every enum (Kind, Fidelity, MeasureUnit, MeasureSemantics, AnchorConfidence, TemporalKind, FidelityLevel) carries its own [JsonConverter(typeof(JsonStringEnumConverter<T>))] with no naming policy, so enum *values* serialize in their literal C# casing ("Method", "Exact", "Interval", "Full"), not camelCase. Property names are camelCase; enum values are PascalCase. Both are correct — do not 'fix' one to match the other.

NOTE 2 — $kind vs kind: EntityRef's [JsonPolymorphic] discriminator ($kind, e.g. "method") is only emitted when a value is serialized through a property declared as the abstract EntityRef type — which is only true for Observation.Subjects. A field declared as a concrete subtype (MethodRef.DeclaringType : TypeRef, TypeRef.Module : ModuleRef?) never gets a $kind, even though it carries the same 'kind' property. A consumer parsing entities nested inside subjects (declaringType, module) must not expect $kind there.

NOTE 3 — 64-bit handles as JSON numbers: ulong fields (ObjectRef.Address, TypeRef.MethodTable, MethodRef.MethodDesc, ModuleRef.ModuleAddress) serialize as plain JSON numeric literals with full precision. A JS/TS consumer using JSON.parse will silently lose precision above 2^53 — heap addresses on a 64-bit process routinely exceed that. Any UI/Phase 8 consumer must parse these as strings or a BigInt-safe parser, not JSON.parse's default number handling.
TimeSpan fields (TimeAnchor.ProcessUptime) serialize via .NET's constant ('c') TimeSpan format, e.g. "00:00:01" or "1.02:03:04.5000000" for a value spanning more than a day.

HISTORICAL (fixed in 2.0.0, 2026-09-10): ArtifactId, Capability, and ObservationId used to serialize as one-key wrapper objects ({"value":"..."} / {"key":"..."}), never as bare JSON strings — and ObservationId's wrapped Guid used the default 'D' format (hyphenated), silently disagreeing with what ObservationId.ToString() printed ('N' format, no hyphens). All three now carry a custom JsonConverter and serialize as bare strings; ObservationId's JSON form now matches its ToString() exactly. See docs/refactor/modularity/phase-1-sdk-review-findings.md items 8 and 9.

idString.description: ArtifactId, Capability, or ObservationId — each a bare JSON string as of schemaVersion 2.0.0 (see the HISTORICAL note above for the pre-2.0.0 wrapper-object shape). ObservationId's string form is Guid 'N' format (no hyphens, e.g. "5dedca19ade345b7bed6726f92d31d80"), matching its ToString() exactly. Capability values must be members of capability-registry.json.

typeRefBody.description: TypeRef fields when nested via a concretely-typed property (no $kind — see NOTE 2).

entityRef.description: Only shape used for Observation.Subjects elements — carries $kind (see NOTE 2).

measure.description: Must be a raw fact, never a weighted composite — see Observation.cs's purity-rules remark.

observationType.description: Free-form per Observation.cs by design; the checked-in list of types actually emitted today lives in observation-type-registry.json, not as a closed enum here.
